ANC, in collaboration with an energy auditor, adjusted the project scope to fit a reduced budget, which included upgrades in HVAC (replacing thermostats and improving hydronic heating systems) and lighting (replacing with LED). In June 2023, the NREL project manager contacted multiple HVAC and electrical engineering vendors, receiving three HVAC bids and one electrical bid by the July deadline. ANC selected the most cost-effective HVAC bid with guidance from the energy auditor and negotiated additional work with the electrical vendor, leading to a modified bid by late July. The selected retrofits—LED lighting replacements, programmable thermostats, and hydronic heating system improvements (Table 1)—were chosen because of their 4 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. estimated high-impact potential for energy savings and operational cost reduction, informed by the previous energy audits and industry-standard recommendations. 2.1 Pre-construction detailed scope of work: Staff completed a comprehensive scope of work for each building. 2.2 Write an RFP for each scope of work and solicit bids: RFPs were released incorporating technical requirements and performance minimums. 2.3 Finalize contractor selection and obtain quotes: After scaling back on the number of buildings, the winning bid was selected and the contract finalized for the scope of work on one building. Necessary materials were ordered; the maintenance director prepared the facility for construction and was present during the installation of new systems and equipment. Obtaining vendor approval from the DOE was delayed (even with assistance from DOE staff), and it was not until late December 2023 that contracted vendors were ready to start. Weather and supply chain issues, and unanticipated boiler issues delayed the completion until June 2024. The project faced numerous challenges, particularly because of Akiachak’s remote location, compounded by weather conditions and transportation logistics (Figure 2).
